lessons.title: Past tense: درستُ
lessons.learn: The past wears SUFFIXES! درستُ (I studied), درستَ (you-m studied), درستِ (you-f studied), درسَ (he studied), درسَتْ (she studied). One stem درسـ + five tails. Your tail tells who!

grammar.title: Past suffixes: -تُ/-تَ/-تِ/-َ/-َتْ
grammar.explain: درستُ (I), درستَ (you-m), درستِ (you-f), درسَ (he), درسَتْ (she). She adds -تْ to his form! Negate past with ما: ما درستُ = I didn't study.
mistakes: Saying درستَ for 'I studied' — I takes درستُ!
Saying هو درستْ — HE takes درسَ (no ت)!

lessons.title: Future: سأدرس
lessons.learn: Two futures! سـ + present (سأدرس = I will study) for quick plans, سوف + present (سوف أدرس) for bigger ones. Just glue سـ onto the present verb — done!

grammar.title: سـ / سوف + present
grammar.explain: سأدرس (I will study), ستدرس (you will), سيدرس (he will). سوف أدرس = same, grander. Negate future with لن: لن أذهب = I won't go.
mistakes: Gluing سـ to the PAST: سـ loves PRESENT verbs!
Negating future with ما — future needs لن!

dialogue.en: What will you do tomorrow? (to m)
I will study Arabic. And you? (to f)

lessons.title: Pinning time: أمس، الآن، غداً
lessons.learn: Arabic often lets the time word carry what English does with tense: أمس with a perfect verb, غداً with سـ, الآن with the present. Put the time word first and it frames everything after it.

grammar.title: Time word + tense
grammar.pattern: time word first + verb in the matching form
grammar.explain: غداً سأدرس (tomorrow I will study). أمس درستُ (yesterday I studied). الآن أدرس (now I am studying). The time word does not change the verb — but it must agree with it.

examples.en: Tomorrow I will travel to Dubai.
We always drink coffee in the morning.

mistakes.why: غداً cannot sit with a past verb.
A frequency word and a one-time past word contradict each other.

dialogue.t: درستُ ثمّ شربتُ القهوة مع صديقتي.

dialogue.en: I studied, then drank coffee with my friend.
And what will you do tomorrow?

dialogue.r: ghadan sa-azūr jaddatī, wa-baʿda qalīl attaṣil bihā.
dialogue.en: Tomorrow I will visit my grandmother, and in a little while I'll call her.

lessons.title: Adjectives: الكتاب الكبير
lessons.learn: Describe everything! Adjectives FOLLOW nouns and MATCH: الكتاب الكبير (the big book), السيارة الكبيرة (the big car-f). ال on BOTH words! Without ال: كتاب كبير (a big book) — match but no ال!

grammar.title: Noun + matching adjective
grammar.explain: كتاب كبير (a big book), الكتاب الكبير (THE big book). Feminine: سيارة كبيرة. Sun letters (ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن) swallow the L: الشارع = ash-shāriʿ!
grammar.pattern: noun + adj (both ال or both bare)
mistakes: Saying الكتاب كبير for 'the big book' — needs الكتاب الكبير!
Saying سيارة كبير — feminine needs كبيرة!

lessons.title: Places: في، إلى، من
lessons.learn: Move around! في (in/at), إلى (to), من (from): في البيت (at home), إلى المدرسة (to school), من مصر (from Egypt). أين؟ (where?) vs إلى أين؟ (where to?) — tiny إلى, big difference!

grammar.title: في / إلى / من
grammar.explain: أنا في البيت (I'm at home), أذهب إلى المدرسة (I go to school), أنا من مصر (I'm from Egypt). Verbs of going demand إلى!
mistakes: Saying أذهب في المدرسة — going needs إلى!
Saying أنا إلى مصر for origin — from = من!

lessons.title: My neighbourhood: في الحيّ
lessons.learn: Places live inside في، على، قريب من and بعيد عن. Tell someone where you live and what is around you, and you can hold a whole conversation on a street corner.

grammar.title: Places and their prepositions
grammar.pattern: fī + place · qarīb min + place · baʿīd ʿan + place
grammar.explain: قريب and بعيد are adjectives, so they agree: الحديقة قريبة من بيتي. When they take من/عن they become a fixed frame: قريب من السوق، بعيد عن المركز.

examples.en: I live in a small neighbourhood.
The mosque is close to our house.
The market is a little far from the university.

mistakes.why: Cities take في; على is 'on' a surface.

dialogue.t: أسكن في حيّ هادئ قريب من الحديقة.
dialogue.r: askun fī ḥayy hādiʾ qarīb min al-ḥadīqa.
dialogue.en: I live in a quiet neighbourhood close to the park.

dialogue.t: نعم، دقيقتان على القدمين، والمسجد أبعد قليلاً.
dialogue.r: naʿam, daqīqatān ʿalā al-qadamayn, wa-l-masjid abʿad qalīlan.
dialogue.en: Yes, two minutes on foot; the mosque is a bit further.

lessons.title: At the restaurant: order, then ask for the bill
lessons.learn: Three moves carry a whole meal: أريد… من فضلك (I want… please), هل عندكم…؟ (do you have…?) and الحساب من فضلك (the bill, please). Add لذيذ and you can talk about it afterwards too.

grammar.title: Ordering frames
grammar.pattern: urīd + noun (+ min faḍlik) · hal ʿindakum + noun?
grammar.explain: أريد دجاجاً من فضلك. Do you want it with something? بـ: أريد دجاجاً بالأرز. To ask what exists, use هل عندكم…؟

examples.en: Do you have coffee without sugar?

mistakes.why: Asking for the bill uses من فضلك, not شكراً.

dialogue.en: Good evening, what would you like?

dialogue.t: أريد دجاجاً بالأرز، وقهوة من فضلك.
dialogue.r: urīd dajājan bi-l-aruzz, wa-qahwa min faḍlik.
dialogue.en: I want chicken with rice, and a coffee please.
Would you like a salad too?

dialogue.t: لا، شكراً. الطعام لذيذ، والحساب من فضلك.
dialogue.r: lā, shukran. al-ṭaʿām ladhīdh, wa-l-ḥisāb min faḍlik.
dialogue.en: No thanks. The food is delicious — and the bill, please.

culture.text: The Arabic past tense is not only 'past': with قد and the perfect form it also reports news the listener has not heard yet, which is why the same sentence can mean 'he wrote' and 'he has written'. Learners who translate word-for-word miss that the verb form is doing the work of an English tense-and-aspect pair, and Arabic instead leans on time words — أمس، الآن، غداً — to place the action.

reading.text: أمس ذهبتُ إلى السوق مع أخي. اشتريتُ خبزاً وفاكهة، ثمّ شربنا القهوة في مقهى صغير. قال لي: «سأسافر غداً إلى بيروت». سألتُ: «لماذا؟» فأجاب: «لأنّ عملي هناك». في المساء درسنا معاً، ونحن الآن متعبان قليلاً.
reading.gloss: Yesterday I went to the market with my brother. I bought bread and fruit, then we drank coffee in a small café. He told me, 'I will travel tomorrow to Beirut.' I asked, 'Why?' and he answered, 'Because my work is there.' In the evening we studied together; we are a little tired now.

listening.script:
أ: بكم هذا الكتاب؟
ب: عشرون جنيهاً.
أ: غالي قليلاً. وهذه الحقيبة؟
ب: خمسة وثلاثون. كل شيء عندنا بخمسة وثلاثين وأربعين.
أ: حسناً، آخذ الاثنين.
listening.gloss: A: How much is this book? B: Twenty pounds. A: A little expensive. And this bag? B: Thirty-five. Everything we have is thirty-five or forty. A: Fine, I'll take both.

idioms.literal: in the blink of an eye

idioms.meaning: in full swing, at full speed
the watchword; the key to something

mistakes.why: The perfect ending -تُ already means 'I'; keeping أنا is not wrong but sounds heavy in a plain past narrative.
سـ marks the future only; it cannot sit with أمس.

mistakes.wrong: هذا الكتاب كبير والكتاب هذا كبير أيضاً.
mistakes.right: هذا الكتاب كبير وهذا الكتاب كبير أيضاً.
mistakes.why: Two full noun phrases need a joining و and one demonstrative each; repeating the whole phrase without a connector is a run-on.

task.title: Yesterday and tomorrow, in writing
task.instructions: Write five Arabic sentences: three about yesterday with perfect-tense endings, two about tomorrow with سـ or سوف. Then say them aloud without reading, and circle any sentence where you used أنا with a past verb — that is the habit this lesson breaks.
